title: Toba supereruption
summary: About 74,000 years ago the Toba volcano in northern Sumatra erupted in what is described as the largest eruption of the past two million years, throwing ash high into the air. How far it cooled the climate and whether it affected early human populations are debated; a 2021 modelling study found strong Northern Hemisphere cooling but milder effects in Africa.

uncertainty.note: Sources say only "about 74,000 years ago"; the plus/minus figure is a placeholder width, not a published uncertainty. Years are 1950 minus the age.

as_recorded.value: the largest volcanic eruption in the past two million years

where.modern_name: Lake Toba (Toba caldera), North Sumatra, Indonesia
where.historical_name: Toba volcano, Sumatra; no states or place names exist at this date

importance.justification: The largest known eruption of the last two million years, central to debates about volcanic effects on climate and early human populations.
